note: Patrick Mahomes broke out of his funk last week with 25.4 fantasy points (QB5 for the week). I didn't see that coming against Denver. It was Mahomes' first game with more than 17 fantasy points since Week 2. Overall, he is the QB14 in fantasy points per game. Mahomes continues to operate as a low aDOT machine. Among 30 qualifying passers, he is ninth in yards per attempt, fourth in passing success rate, and tenth in fantasy points per dropback, but he also has the highest rate of passing yards coming from yards after the catch (66.6%) and the lowest aDOT (6.11). Mahomes should have another QB1 outing this week against a struggling Jets pass defense. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the tenth-most yards per attempt, the fifth-highest passing success rate, the sixth-highest passing touchdown rate, and the fifth-most fantasy points per dropback.

Since his Week 5 return, Jayden Daniels has been the QB5 in fantasy points per game. During those three games, he has averaged five rushing attempts and 45.3 yards on the ground (two rushing scores). Among 30 qualifying passers, Daniels is 20th in yards per attempt, 24th in passing success rate, 16th in catchable target rate, and 15th in highly accurate throw rate. Daniels will need a nice rushing performance this week to pay off for fantasy. The Rams pass defense has remained tough over their last five games, allowing the eighth-lowest EPA per dropback, the tenth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-lowest passing success rate, and the 14th-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

Jordan Love is the QB10 in fantasy points per game. Love has multiple passing touchdowns in every game except one, while surpassing 280 passing yards in four games. Among 30 qualifying passers, Love is 14th in yards per attempt, 19th in passing success rate, first in deep ball rate, and 11th in hero throw rate. Love should have another QB1 outing this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the sixth-most yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passing success rate, and the seventh-most EPA per dropback.

Matthew Stafford is the QB16 in fantasy points per game with four weeks with at least 18.5 fantasy points. Stafford has four 300-yard passing days this season and five games with multiple passing touchdowns. Among 30 qualifying passers, Stafford is 16th in yards per attempt, tenth in passing success rate, 20th in catchable target rate, and 23rd in hero throw rate. Washington has had some improvements over the last few weeks as a pass defense, but this is still just a middle-of-the-road pass defense. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the third-highest CPOE while ranking 15th in passing success rate, 18th in EPA per dropback, and 16th in fantasy points per dropback. Stafford could easily post a nice QB1 day in Week 9.

Tyler Shough is the QB12 in fantasy points per game. Among 30 qualifying passers, Shough is 24th in yards per attempt, 17th in passing success rate, ninth in catchable target rate, and seventh in hero throw rate. The Saints rely on Shough's arm weekly to move the ball as their rushing offense has been non-existent. Shough (even after a bye week) is seventh in passing attempts and tenth in dropbacks. Shough will have a tough battle on hands this week. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the ninth-fewest yards per attempt, the tenth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the fourth-lowest passing success rate, and the tenth-fewest EPA per dropback.

C.J. Stroud is the QB14 in fantasy points per game with three games this season with at least 20.9 fantasy points. Stroud could easily make that four after this week. Stroud has multiple passing touchdowns in four games this season and managed 300 passing yards three times. Among 30 qualifying passers, Stroud has been dealing, ranking 11th in yards per attempt, 14th in passing success rate, seventh in highly accurate throw rate, and first in hero throw rate. Over their last five games, the Bolts have been a middle-of-the-road pass defense, ranking 16th in yards per attempt, 13th in passing success rate, and 18th in CPOE.

Since Week 5, Malik Willis has been the QB7 in fantasy points per game. Last week, his production fell back to Earth as his rushing disappeared again. Willis ran only once with two yards. I simply don't understand why Miami isn't utilizing his legs and talents as a runner on a weekly basis, but at this point of the season his weekly volatility with his rushing will help or hurt his fantasy output. Willis has three games where he hasn't managed more than 12 rushing yards this season. Since Week 5, among 32 qualifying passers, we have seen growth as a passer as he has ranked 16th in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, seventh in highly accurate throw rate, and 16th in catchable target rate. Willis could post another QB1 outing this week. Across their last five games, Detroit has allowed the 14th-most yards per attempt, the sixth-highest passing touchdown rate, the fourth-highest passing success rate, and the 12th-highest CPOE.

Kirk Cousins has been BALLING as the QB5 in fantasy points per game. Among 30 qualifying passers, Cousins is 12th in yards per attempt, eighth in passing success rate, 22nd in catchable target rate, and 18th in hero throw rate. Cousins is third in passing yards and second to only Joe Burrow in passing yards among all quarterbacks. Cousins has multiple passing touchdowns in every game this season except for one. This week, he gets a neutral matchup against the 49ers, who, over their last five games, have ranked 16th in passing success rate and EPA per dropback and have allowed the 14th-highest passing touchdown rate.

Over the last two weeks, Bo Nix has been the QB3 and QB12 in weekly scoring. Overall, he's the QB24 in fantasy points per game. I wish I could tell you that his level of play has massively improved, but that's not the case. Over the last two weeks, among 25 qualifying passers, Nix is 11th in yards per attempt and 12th in aDOT, but he is also 25th in passing success rate, 18th in highly accurate throw rate, and has the fifth-highest off-target rate. Yeah, it looks like more of the same from Nix. He could easily be a decent QB2 this week, but I wouldn't expect much more than that. Over their last five games, Carolina has been a middle-of-the-road matchup for passers, ranking 15th in fantasy points per dropback while giving up the tenth-highest CPOE and 12th-most EPA per dropback.

After posting 20 or more fantasy points in back-to-back games entering Week 8, Michael Penix managed to have a massive dud game against the Bucs. Penix completed only eight of 24 passes with four interceptions and 5.2 yards per attempt. It was an absolute nightmare fuel performance. With all that said, this is a good bounce-back spot for Penix. Overall, among 30 qualifying passers, Penix is tenth in yards per attempt, 15th in passing success rate, 27th in highly accurate throw rate, and he has the highest turnover-worthy throw rate. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the seventh-most yards per attempt, the ninth-highest passing touchdown rate, the sixth-highest passing success rate, and the 11th-most fantasy points per dropback. Penix could return to solid QB2 production this week.

In his last two games of action for the Giants, J.J. McCarthy was the QB12 and QB23 in weekly fantasy scoring. The QB23 finish doesn't do his level of play justice. Among 40 qualifying passers, McCarthy is first in yards per attempt, first in aDOT, 17th in passing success rate, fourth in catchable target rate, and first in hero throw rate. The Eagles' pass defense has shown cracks in the pavement, and McCarthy can take advantage this week. Over the last five games, Philly has allowed the 12th-highest yards per attempt and the eighth-highest EPA per dropback, while ranking 17th in passing touchdown rate. During that span, Philly has also had issues with deep passing, giving up the tenth-highest passing success rate and the third-most deep passing yards. Among those 40 qualifying passers, McCarthy is first in deep ball rate by a mile with 18.4%. The Eagles have also had the third-lowest pressure rate and the second-lowest quick pressure rate in that span. Chef McCarthy should have time in the kitchen to cook again this week.

With Sam Darnold sidelined with a quad injury, Drew Lock will make a start for Seattle. Funny enough, his last start of the season was against the Cardinals. In that game, he completed 73.1% of his passes with 235 yards through the air and three passing scores. Lock was the QB9 in weekly scoring that week. This season, among 40 qualifying passers, Lock is third in yards per attempt, seventh in highly accurate throw rate, 22nd in catchable target rate, and 11th in hero throw rate. Lock could have another QB1-level stat line this week. Arizona's pass defense has been horrible. Over their last five games, the Cards have allowed the ninth-most yards per attempt, the fifth-highest passing touchdown rate, the sixth-most EPA per dropback, and the second-most fantasy points per dropback.

Over the last two games, Bryce Young has looked more like last season's Young, as the QB24 and QB18 in weekly scoring. In those two games, among 25 qualifying passers, Young has ranked 24th in yards per attempt, 19th in highly accurate throw rate, 17th in catchable target rate, and 23rd in fantasy points per dropback. I don't think this is the week Young gets it back on track (if he does). Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per attempt, the 13th-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-fewest fantasy points per dropback, and the tenth-fewest EPA per dropback.

Since his return to the lineup, Baker Mayfield has averaged only seven passing attempts and 32 passing yards per game. Yes, I know the weather was a factor in one of those games, but Mayfield hasn't been good with the passing attempts he has had since his return. Since Week 7, he has had only 4.5 yards per attempt, a 6.58 aDOT, and a 42.9% highly accurate throw rate. I expect him to pass more out of necessity this week, but I also expect the Bucs to hide him as much as possible. Sit Mayfield and fade this passing attack overall.

Carson Wentz will draw the start for Minnesota this week. In Wentz's two games of action this season, he was the QB12 and QB30 in weekly scoring. Among 42 qualifying passers this season, Wentz is 20th in yards per attempt, 37th in passing success rate, 40th in highly accurate throw rate, and 37th in catchable target rate. Wentz likely isn't the savior for this offense and passing attack. His accuracy issues have been substantial. The thing working in Wentz's favor is the fact that the Bills' pass defense hasn't been a unit to be scared of this season. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the 13th-highest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-highest passing success rate, the 13th-most EPA per dropback, and the 15th-most fantasy points per dropback. Wentz can post serviceable QB2 numbers this week.

Daniel Jones is the QB37 in fantasy points per game. Just let that soak in for a second. He has managed more than 13 fantasy points only once this season. It has been a spectacular struggle bus for Jones and the Colts' offense. Among 30 qualifying passers, Jones is 29th in yards per attempt, 21st in passing success rate, 25th in highly accurate throw rate, and dead last in hero throw rate. I don't have any faith in Jones at all, but maybe Dallas can allow him to post a decent stat line this week. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 11th-most yards per attempt, the 14th-highest passer rating, the eighth-highest CPOE, and the tenth-most EPA per dropback.

I don't see a reason for hope for Justin Herbert at this point. He hasn't passed for more than 260 yards in any game this season. Herbert has zero games with multiple passing touchdowns, and he has thrown an interception in every game this season. Herbert is QB34 in fantasy points per game with zero games with 15 or more fantasy points. I need a prove-it game before I'm willing to plug him into any fantasy lineup.

After last week's QB13 finish, Geno Smith is the QB20 in fantasy points per game with three games of at least 19 fantasy points under his belt. Among 30 qualifying passers, Smith is sixth in yards per attempt, 11th in passing success rate, 14th in highly accurate throw rate, and fifth in catchable target rate. Smith has been a very good streaming option when the matchup has presented itself. Well, the matchup is horrible this week. Sit Smith. Across their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate and passing success rate, the 14th-fewest yards per attempt, and the 11th-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

With Deshaun Watson dealing with a concussion, Shedeur Sanders will be the starting quarterback for the Browns this week. Last year, in Weeks 12-18, with Sanders starting, he was a QB1 in weekly scoring only once. Last year, among 38 qualifying passers, Sanders was 30th in yards per attempt, 37th in passing success rate, and 23rd in hero throw rate. Yes, I know there's not much to be positive about in that sample, but we did see flashes from Sanders with a 364 passing yard outing (three passing scores) against the Titans. Sanders also had at least 20 rushing yards in each of his final five games last year, so there's some rushing production here to chew on. Last year, it was tough to evaluate Sanders behind a patchwork offensive line and with only Harold Fannin to throw to as a serviceable pass catcher at times. Sanders has a rebuilt offensive line to operate behind this season and plenty of skill talent around him. The Saints' pass defense has been horrible. Sanders should post solid QB2 numbers this week, and I wouldn't be surprised if he flirted with low-end QB1 production. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the fourth-most yards per attempt, the 11th-highest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-highest passing success rate, and the tenth-most fantasy points per dropback.

Tanner McKee has been benched. Joe Milton will now be the starting quarterback for the Eagles. We'll see if he can hold the job for the rest of the season. Since 2024, Milton has only had 57 regular-season dropbacks to work with as a sample size. With those dropbacks, Milton has had 8.1 yards per attempt, a 53.8% passing success rate, a 13.5% deep ball rate, an 80.9% catchable target rate, and a 5.8% hero throw rate. Those are all solid, if not STRONG, numbers. Again, this is an incredibly small sample, but it at least paints a picture of optimism, which I don't think we can say existed for McKee after what we've seen this season. This week, he'll have a tough matchup against the Giants, but he could still return serviceable QB2 production. Over their last five games, the Giants have allowed the second-fewest yards per attempt, the third-lowest passing success rate, the seventh-lowest CPOE, and the sixth-lowest EPA per dropback.

Last week, Gardner Minshew was a JJ McCarthy-level hero. He led the Cards to a win against Dallas after taking over for Jacoby Brissett. He completed 17 of 23 passes with 188 passing yards (8.2 yards per attempt) and three scores. I love the mustache maestro, but he comes crashing back to Earth this week against Seattle. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per attempt and fantasy points per dropback, the sixth-lowest passing success rate, and the fifth-fewest EPA per dropback. Minshew will have streamable weeks, but this isn't one of them.

Baltimore's third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano will be starting this week for the Ravens. Last week, with injuries to Tyler Huntley and Lamar Jackson, he was pressed into duty. The team just traded for Jacoby Brissett, but he won't have enough time to take the starting job this week. He finished with 21 passing attempts, a 47.6% completion rate, 91 passing yards (one pick), and 4.3 yards per attempt. This preseason, he had some success. Among 62 qualifying passers, he was 22nd in yards per attempt and ninth in adjusted completion rate with a 3:1 passing touchdown-to-interception ratio. Fagnano also had the tenth-lowest aDOT. If he can even be a league-average game manager this week, it should be considered a win for Baltimore. Adding to all of this, he is playing through an ankle injury. He's a low-end QB2 with a rough matchup. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the eighth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-lowest passing success rate, and the seventh-lowest EPA per dropback.

Chase Brown is the RB20 in fantasy points per game just based on volume alone. He has one touchdown all season, and he has averaged 18.5 touches and 75.6 total yards. Brown's role has remained consistent with 75.5% and 68.9% snap rates over the last two games. Overall, he has a 71.4% snap rate with 61.4% of the rushing work, a 57.8% route share, and a 15% target share. Brown has posted a solid 2.21 yards after contact per attempt while also having a disappointing 13% missed tackle rate and 8% explosive run rate. His offensive line hasn't done him many favors with only 1.40 yards before contact per attempt. This week's matchup could finally lead to Brown's first 100-yard day on the ground, though. The Falcons' run defense has fallen off a cliff. In their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two games, Jonathan Taylor has seen his workload scaled back with a 66.4% snap rate, 44.1% of the rushing work, and a 54.7% route share (15.4% target share). In those games, Taylor has averaged 16 touches and 78.5 total yards. Overall, Taylor has a strong 13.7% explosive run rate and 16% missed tackle rate. Even in a reduced capacity, Taylor should have a nice day against Dallas. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the second-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the third-most yards before contact per attempt, and the sixth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Rhamondre Stevenson remains New England's workhorse back. Stevenson is the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 14.9 touches and 72.4 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, Stevenson is 26th in yards after contact per attempt and seventh in missed tackle rate. Stevenson is a volume-based RB2 again this week. Across their last five games, Green Bay has ranked 15th in rushing success rate while allowing the 12th-most yards after contact per attempt and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate.

In Week 7, Jonah Coleman led the backfield in snaps (50%), rushing attempts (nine, 34.6%), and was second in route share (21.9%), running one less route than RJ Harvey. Coleman finished with 11 touches and 69 total yards. Last week, his role grew further with RJ Harvey out. Coleman finished with 15 touches and 104 total yards (RB12 for the week) with a 67.9% snap rate, a 47.8% rushing share, and a 50% route share (12.5% target share). This season, among 58 qualifying rushers, Coleman is first in explosive run rate and 19th in missed tackle rate. Coleman is a wonderful fantasy option this week, and he could continue to crush. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Week 4, Ollie Gordon has been the RB16 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.6 touches and 90 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, Gordon is eighth in explosive run rate and 23rd in yards after contact per attempt. The only drawback to Gordon has been the lack of passing game involvement. Over his last four games, he has only six targets and zero receiving yards. He has to get it done on early downs, which he has been doing. Gordon will find more uphill sledding this week, though. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the eighth-lowest rushing success rate, the fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt. He'll need a touchdown to pay off for fantasy this week, along with all the volume he can handle.

Since Week 6, as the starting back for Houston, Woody Marks has been the RB35 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.5 touches and 74.3 total yards. With that type of volume, the biggest culprit for underperforming in fantasy is the fact that he didn't have a touchdown in either game. In those two games, he played 83.2% of the snaps with 68% of the rushing work and a 56.9% route share (6.5% target share). Among 42 qualifying backs, he is 21st in explosive run rate and 18th in missed tackle rate. Marks is a volume-based RB2 with a good matchup this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the tenth-most yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, Quinshon Judkins had a season-low 39.1% snap rate with 73.3% of the rushing work and only an 18% route share (4.9% target share). In the first seven weeks of the season, Judkins had a 59.2% snap rate and a 30.3% route share. We'll see if this role reduction holds this week, but it's a worry for Judkins moving forward. Judkins is the RB23 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15.4 touches and 68 total yards. Among 45 qualifying backs, he is 37th in explosive run rate, 39th in yards after contact per attempt, and 32nd in missed tackle rate. If the Browns play with a lead this week, they could load up Judkins with rushing volume. If that happens, he'll have a nice stat line. The Saints have been unable to stop the run. Over their last five games, they have allowed the seventh-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 13th-highest missed tackle rate.

Derrick Henry might be the RB13 in fantasy points per game overall, but that doesn't tell the entire story. Since Week 4, without Lamar Jackson, he has been the RB28 in fantasy points per game, averaging 19.8 touches and 73.6 total yards. Among 42 qualifying backs, he is still performing well, ranking 18th in explosive run rate and 17th in yards after contact per attempt. Henry is now a volume-based RB2 with a horrible matchup this week. Yes, Jacksonville just lost DaVon Hamilton, but they should still field a solid, if not strong, run defense. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the third-lowest explosive run rate, the lowest rushing success rate, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Ashton Jeanty was turned into the passing-down-only back with a 36.7% snap rate, only two rushing attempts, a 48.1% route share, and an 11.5% target share. I don't know if this is the beginning of a new role for him or punishment for mouthing off to the media about the Jets' run defense. We'll have to wait and see what his usage looks like in Week 9. In Weeks 1-7, Jeanty had a 69.5% snap rate, 60.9% of the rushing work, and a 54.8% route share (16.5% target share). Last week, Jeanty finished with five touches and 73 total yards. In Weeks 1-7, Jeanty averaged 20 touches and 91.5 total yards (RB14 in fantasy points per game). This season, Jeanty has 2.13 yards after contact per attempt, which is solid, but he has also logged a 12% missed tackle rate and 5.1% explosive run rate. Those last two stats won't get it done, but we also have to remember he has been playing through injury and behind an offensive line that has been putrid. The Raiders rank dead last in yards before contact per attempt (0.97). The Packers are 31st, and they have generated 1.28 yards before contact per attempt just for context. Jeanty has a wide range of outcomes this week, but even if his previous role comes back, he has a tough matchup. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-lowest missed tackle rate.

Devin Singletary will operate as the Giants' workhorse this week, with only Singletary and Greg Desrosiers healthy in the running back room. This season, in limited duty, Singletary has posted a solid 2.11 yards after contact per attempt and a 17% missed tackle rate. He should flirt with 15-18 touches this week with a nice matchup incoming. Singletary is an RB2 this week. Over the last five games, Philly's run defense has been leaky, allowing the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-highest rushing success rate, the eighth-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Saquon Barkley played only 32.4% of the snaps with a 44.8% rushing share and a 16.3% route share (2.9% target share). Last week, Barkley finished with 14 touches and 54 total yards (one touchdown). Barkley was the RB22 in weekly scoring. In the last two weeks, Barkley has had an 11.8% explosive run rate, 2.55 yards after contact per attempt, and a 20% missed tackle rate. These are all amazing numbers considering Barkley has been playing with one healthy leg and a balky back. Barkley can get it done this week on limited volume. Over the last five games, New York has allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 15th-most yards after contact per attempt. Barkley opened the week with a DNP.

Last week, Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight got injured, and Tyler Allgeier became the team's bell-cow runner against Dallas. Allgeier responded with 16 touches and 191 total yards (two scores) as the RB1 for the week. I don't expect that type of output from Allgeier moving forward, especially this week, but he will be a volume-fueled running back option for lineups. Among 42 qualifying backs, Allgeier is first in yards after contact per attempt and 31st in missed tackle rate. This week, he'll need all the volume he can handle and a touchdown to pay off for fantasy. Seattle has shut down rushers. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-lowest explosive run rate, the 11th-lowest rushing success rate, and the eighth-fewest yards before contact per attempt.

Since Week 5, Alvin Kamara has had a 36.9% snap rate, 22.2% of the rushing work, and a 32.3% route share (14% target share). Since Week 5, he has averaged nine touches and 45.7 total yards. In those three games, he has had a 12.5% explosive run rate, 2.19 yards after contact per attempt, and a 31% missed tackle rate. Those numbers imply Kamara is getting healthier because he hasn't posted numbers like that until this point in the season. Kamara could surprise with a strong showing this week. The Browns have been bleeding out production to backs. Over their last five games, they have allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, and the second-highest yards after contact per attempt and missed tackle rate. With Kendre Miller released, I expect Kamara's role to grow this week.

Last week, Rachaad White had to deal with Jeremy McNichols and Austin Ekeler cutting into his workload. With McNichols placed on IR, White will likely only have to deal with Ekeler this week, but Robert Henry Jr. could get into the mix, and I wouldn't be shocked. Last week, White played 47.4% of the snaps with 42.3% of the rushing work and a 39.4% route share (10.3% target share). White finished with 12 touches and 60 total yards (one score) as the RB15 for the week. White has posted a solid 17% missed tackle rate this season but a disappointing 1.87 yards after contact per attempt. White will need to make the most of his volume and likely get into the endzone to pay off for fantasy this week. The matchup is rough. The Rams' run defense has improved. Over the last five games, they have allowed the 13th-lowest rushing success rate, the 11th-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the fourth-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the sixth-lowest missed tackle rate.

Breece Hall will be back this week. With that said, I don't know what to do with the Jets backfield. I can envision an easy scenario where Hall is immediately reinstalled as the Jets' workhorse this week, but I can also understand if New York wants to deploy a committee or have a hot hand approach this week. Braelon Allen was absolutely awesome with Hall out, so it's likely tough to put that tackle-breaking genie back in the bottle. Among 42 qualifying backs, Hall is 20th in explosive run rate, 41st in yards after contact per attempt, and 27th in missed tackle rate. Hall hasn't been immensely efficient with his workload this season even before dealing with the injury. With workload questions this week, Hall needs to be as efficient as possible with his touches, but that will be tough against the Chiefs' stout run defense. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the second-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt. Hall could be a volume-based RB2 this week or a touchdown-needy RB3/flex.

Last week, Jadarian Price surprisingly led the backfield with a 48.2% snap rate, a 52.6% rushing share, and a 33.3% route share. Price finished with 12 touches and 37 total yards. The red zone work was split up between Price and Zach Charbonnet, with Price seeing one carry inside the 20-yard line while Charbonnet had two. Price has been efficient with his workload this season with 2.55 yards after contact per attempt and a 24% missed tackle rate. I have no clue if he'll continue to lead the way for Seattle's ground game, though. That was Zach Charbonnet's first game back in the lineup, and I expect his role to grow moving forward. Price will need volume this week and a score to pay off as a flex this week. Arizona's run defense has massively improved. Over their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Blake Corum is on fire! Since Week 5, he has been the RB13 in fantasy points per game, averaging 12 touches and 76.6 total yards. Corum has scored a touchdown in each of his last four games. Among 42 qualifying backs, Corum is seventh in explosive run rate and 17th in missed tackle rate. This could be the week that Corum's hot streak ends, though. Over their last five games, Washington has tightened up the run defense, allowing the fifth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

Braelon Allen could immediately return to operating as Breece Hall's understudy, or he could force a committee. Allen was fantastic with Hall out. In Weeks 4-8, Allen averaged 21.2 touches and 114.8 total yards as the RB15 in fantasy points per game. Among 42 qualifying backs, Allen is third in explosive run rate, seventh in yards after contact per attempt, and 14th in missed tackle rate. If the Jets open Week 9 with a hot hand approach with their backfield, don't be surprised if Allen has the warmer mitts. Allen's range of outcomes is wide. He could be a decent RB2 or a touchdown-needy flex this week. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the eighth-lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, and the second-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt.

Last week was Zach Charbonnet's first game back. Charbonnet finished with nine touches and 29 total yards while leading the backfield with two red zone rushing attempts. Charbonnet was second on the team in backfield snap rate (35.7%), rushing share (31.6%), and route share (17.9%). He has only 1.67 yards after contact per attempt but a solid 17% missed tackle rate. Charbonnet's workload is likely to grow moving forward, but I don't want to flex him this week. Arizona's run defense has massively improved. Over their last five games, they have allowed the sixth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, and the seventh-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Over the last two games, Jordan Mason has been the Vikings' lead back, averaging only 12.5 touches and 44 total yards. Mason has had a 46.2% snap rate, 48.9% of the rushing work, and a 24.2% route share. He has led the Minny backfield in each of those categories over the last two games. Mason has posted a disappointing 1.89 yards after contact per attempt and an 8% missed tackle rate this season. With the limited volume and effectiveness, Mason is a touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the Bills have allowed the 12th-highest explosive run rate and rushing success rate, and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two weeks, Aaron Jones has been a committee back with Jordan Mason, averaging eight touches and 33 total yards. In those games, he has had a 32.1% snap rate, 27.7% of the rushing attempts, and a 21% route share. Mason has bested him in each of those categories as Minny's lead back. Jones has shown his age this season with only 1.97 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate. He's a touchdown-dependent flex this week. Over their last five games, the Bills have allowed the 12th-highest explosive run rate and rushing success rate and the sixth-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two games, Dylan Sampson has had a 50.1% snap rate, a 15.9% rushing share, a 47.7% route share, and an 11.7% target share. Sampson has averaged eight touches and 73 total yards. In those two games, Sampson has had a 21% TPRR with an eye-popping 2.24 YPRR and a red zone target. With his minuscule rushing work, he has also had 2.43 yards after contact per attempt and a 14.3 explosive run rate. Sampson is a strong flex play this week, especially in PPR formats. He has been the RB28 and RB19 over the last two weeks. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the third-highest yards per target, the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the tenth-most receiving yards to running backs. Sampson should also be able to make the most of his carries this week. Over their last five games, the Saints have allowed the seventh-highest rushing success rate, the fifth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 13th-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week was just more of the same for Omarion Hampton. He finished with 11 touches and 27 total yards. He had only a 30.5% snap rate, 36% of the rushing work, and an 18.9% route share. If any player not named Omarion Hampton had this lengthy resume of underperformance entering Week 9, he'd be dropped in every league. Hampton has a decent 2.33 yards after contact per attempt, but his 8.6% explosive run rate and 13% missed tackle rate are eye sores. This is another week to sit Hampton. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the 12th-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the 14th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

The Bucs have leaned extremely run-heavy over the last two games. In that span, Kenneth Gainwell has averaged 19.5 carries and 114 rushing yards as the RB35 in fantasy points per game. Gainwell has been awesome on a per-touch basis this season with a 15.5% explosive run rate, 3.09 yards after contact per attempt, and a 29% missed tackle rate. We'll see if the Bucs continue this run-centric offense in Week 9 or if the Bears can pry them away from it, but Gainwell is still a solid flex this week. Last week, the Bears' run defense looked like a force, with Jeffery Simmons clogging up the middle. They allowed only a 26.3% rushing success rate, -0.57 rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and 1.68 yards after contact per attempt. Gainwell won't have an easy road this week, but if he gets 10-15 touches, he can still be flex-worthy.

Mike Washington took over as the team's lead back last week, but I don't know how long that will last. The workload could easily bounce back in the direction of Ashton Jeanty this week if this were all related to his quotes about the Jets' run defense. I have no clue if it's related, but we'll find out how this all shakes out this week. In Weeks 1-7, Washington had a 20.9% snap rate, averaging 6.1 touches and 29.5 total yards. Last week, he played 63.3% of the snaps with 75.8% of the rushing work, and an 18.5% route share. Washington finished with 25 carries and 83 rushing yards. Washington has to run behind the same horrible offensive line that Jeanty does. Washington has managed a 12.3% explosive run rates nd 2.37 yards after contact per attempt, though. Washington's usage and volume are up in the air this week, but he has a horrible matchup incoming and is best left on the bench. Over their last five games, the 49ers have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the second-lowest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-lowest missed tackle rate.

With Bhayshul Tuten active, Chris Rodriguez could still see an elevated role this week. Rodriguez has had a 24.3% snap rate while averaging 6.7 touches and 33.2 total yards. Among 45 qualifying rushers, Rodriguez is 20th in yards after contact per attempt and 15th in missed tackle rate. Rodriguez is a touchdown-dependent flex. Baltimore hasn't been an easy team to run on. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the second-lowest explosive run rate, the seventh-lowest rushing success rate, and the sixth-lowest yards after contact per attempt, but there is a sliver of hope here. Over the same time span, this run defense has also had the fourth-lowest rate of hitting backs at or behind the line of scrimmage, and it has allowed the 11th-highest gap rushing success rate (Rodriguez 53.3% gap).

Christian McCaffrey's hamstring isn't 100%. With McCaffrey operating at less than full health and a nice rushing matchup incoming, I wouldn't be surprised to see Kaelon Black see 12-15 carries against the Raiders. Black has seen at least 12 carries in two games this season while averaging 8.5 touches and 33.9 total yards per game. Black hasn't been impressive as a rusher with only a 7% explosive run rate and 7% missed tackle rate, but that might not matter this week. The Raiders' run defense has been that bad. Over their last five games, Las Vegas has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, the most yards before contact per attempt, and the fifth-highest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two games, with Jonah Coleman leading the way, J.K. Dobbins has seen his role reduced. In those games, Dobbins has had a 22% offensive snap rate with 6.5 rushing attempts and 18 rushing yards per game. Dobbins is a low-end, touchdown-dependent flex until that changes. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the ninth-highest yards before contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Since Caleb Williams' return, Luther Burden has been the WR8 in fantasy points per game with a 20.4% target share, 4.32 YPRR, three red zone targets, a deep target, and a 28.6% first-read share. The only thing that has limited Burden from gaudier numbers is the fact that during that three-game span, he has had only a 56% route share. Burden just shredded Seattle's secondary, so I don't have a ton of concerns about his matchup this week. The Bucs have been quite good against slot receivers, though. Over their last five games, they have allowed the ninth-fewest yards per target to the position while ranking 18th in fantasy points per opportunity. Burden has the talent to overcome another rough-on-paper matchup this week.

Rashee Rice returned to the lineup last week and was the WR9 in weekly scoring. Rice had a 19.5% target share with 1.89 YPRR (53 receiving yards), one red zone target, and a 27.6% first-read share. Rice returned to his low aDOT role with a 4.25 aDOT and a 37.5% designed target rate. Rice could continue the strong production in his old role this week. Since Week 5, the Jets have had the 12th-highest rate of single high (54.5%). Against single high, Rice has had a 22% TPRR with 2.10 YPRR. Over their last five games, the Jets have allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Real talk time. Parker Washington is damn good and has had a bad run, with the Jags blowing out teams. I'm not panicking at all on Washington. Last week, they crushed the Jags while Trevor Lawrence had to throw the ball only 14 times. Against Houston, Washington earned 11 targets and dropped a touchdown. Even going back to the game against Cincy, Washington had to deal with DJ Turner for most of the game, so the disappearing act is understandable. Ok. Rant over. Washington is the WR22 in fantasy points per game with a 22.9% target share (leads the team), 2.47 YPRR, seven red zone targets (leads the team), nine deep targets (leads the team), and a 26.6% first-read share (leads the team). So, just to recap, Washington leads the team in every important metric for pass catchers. This week, Washington gets to face a Baltimore secondary that, over their last five games, has allowed the most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

I'll lead this conversation with I don't know if Patrick Surtain shadows anyone this week. He didn't shadow last week, and I could easily see him not following anyone this week. McMIllan has a 22.6% target share with 2.14 YPRR, six red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 32.7% first-read share. McMillan could see solid volume this week, but I worry about his floor and ceiling against Denver in a game where I worry that we will see Young struggle again. Over the last five games, Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

As I started my discussion about Tetairoa McMillan, I'll lead this conversation with I don't know if Patrick Surtain shadows anyone this week. Over the last five games, Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Jameson Williams has been on a heater. After last week's game, he has risen to the WR18 in fantasy points per game. DJ Moore continues to battle through a gimpy shoulder. Moore will need a healthy dose of volume and a touchdown to overcome the rough matchup this week.

Jaylen Waddle is the WR42 in fantasy points per game, with only three games this season with 14 or more PPR points. Bo Nix has crushed him. This week, he faces a pass defense that has the fifth-highest single high rate (59.3%). Against single high, Waddle has had a 31% TPRR (leads the team) with 1.56 YPRR. Waddle could post a strong stat line this week if Nix can get him the ball. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 5, Ryan Flournoy has been the WR29 in fantasy points per game. In those four games, he has had a 13.8% target share with 1.90 YPRR, four red zone targets, one deep target, and a 12.1% first-read share. Flournoy is in place as a flex again this week, but the matchup isn't as kind as last week. Over their last five games, Indy has allowed the ninth-fewest yards per target and the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Houston has the sixth-highest single high rate (59.1%). This season against single-high, McConkey has had a strong 24% TPRR with 2.83 YPRR. This could be the game where he finally breaks out. Across their last five games, the Texans have allowed the ninth-most yards per target and receiving fantasy points per game.

KC Concepcion is the WR56 in fantasy points per game. Concepcion had a blow-up game against the Titans, but unfortunately he followed it up with a quieter outing last week against the Steelers. Concepcion has an 18.2% target share with 1.57 YPRR, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 25% first-read share (leads the team). The Saints have been ripped apart by slot receivers. Over their last five games, they have allowed the highest yards per target, the ninth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

After two monstrous games, Omar Cooper was held without a target last week despite his 74.3% route share. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchel stole the show. In the two previous games, Cooper was the WR6 and WR9 in weekly scoring. In those games, Cooper had a 20% target share, 4.45 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 29.3% first-read share. Kansas City has the sixth-highest two-high rate in the NFL (59.3%). Since Week 6, against two-high, Cooper has had a 15% TPRR and 1.76 YPRR. Cooper could operate as New York's WR1 this week. With a middle-of-the-road matchup in the slot this week, Cooper could see a heavy workload. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 14th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers while ranking 16th in yards per target.

Last week, Adonai Mitchell was still just a part-time player with a 60.7% snap rate and 71.4% route share. He made the most of his routes with a 28.1% target share (24.6 aDOT), seven receptions, 142 receiving yards, one red zone target, five deep targets, and a 31% first-read share. Mitchell might log back-to-back strong weeks if Geno Smith is willing to test Kansas City's pass defense downfield. With Garrett Wilson out, he could also see a bump in his playing time and usage. The Chiefs have allowed the second-highest passer rating and the third-highest success rate to deep passing this season. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the ninth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 17th in yards per target. Mansoor Delane out this week does make this pass defense a tad less fearsome. Also, another wrinkle working in Mitchell's favor is the Chiefs' love of two-high. Against two-high, Mitchell has excelled with a 25% TPRR and 2.45 YPRR. If Mitchell sees a bump in his usage and connects on some deep targets, he could pop off with another huge game.

Denzel Boston is the WR37 in fantasy points per game with a 20.3% target share, 1.57 YPRR, eight red zone targets, 15 deep targets, and a 24.4% first-read share. Boston has been relatively quiet over the last few weeks. He hasn't managed more than 46 receiving yards in any game since Week 4 and hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 5. This week, he'll face a Saints defense that has the second-highest single high rate in the NFL (65%). Against single high, Boston has only a 15% TPRR with a minuscule 0.57 YPRR. The coverage matchup isn't in his favor, and the corners have been good for the Saints on the perimeter. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the 13th-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Sit Boston this week.

Keenan Allen is the WR38 in fantasy points per game, with three weeks this season with at least 13 PPR points. Allen has a 21.2% target share with 1.80 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 26.2% first-read share. Allen is a viable flex option again this week. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the sixth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Caleb Williams' return, Rome Odunze has been the WR43 in fantasy points per game with a 13.6% target share, 2.03 YPRR, one red zone target, four deep targets, and a 14.3% first-read share. Odunze has been squeezed for targets, with Colston Loveland operating as the alpha and Luther Burden as the number two option. Sit Odunze this week. Over their last five games, the Bucs have allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Malik Washington has been a volume-filled flex this season as the WR40 in fantasy points per game. Last week, Washington finally got into the end zone and finished as the WR14 for the week. It looks like Emeka Egbuka will be back this week. After opening the week with a DNP, he followed it up with full practices on Thursday and Friday. Maybe that changes this week, as they will likely be playing catch-up with the Bears leading. Over their last five games, the Bears have allowed the fourth-most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Williams could be a difference-making player down the stretch for fantasy squads, but I worry about his stat line for Week 9. Tre Tucker is the WR25 in fantasy points per game, with three games with at least 18.8 PPR points this season. Against single-high, Tucker has had a 20% TPRR and 2.01 YPRR. The coverage matchup is in his favor in the sense that Tucker excels against both single and two high, but as far as his downfield role, I don't think he'll have success there. 31.4% of his receiving yardage has been via deep targets, but over their last five games the 49ers have held passers to the 14th-lowest passing success rate and passer rating when targeting 20-plus yards downfield. Also, over their last five games, the 49ers have held perimeter wide receivers to the tenth-fewest yards per target while ranking 15th in fantasy points per opportunity. Sit Tucker this week.

Over the last two weeks, Caleb Douglas has had a 15.1% target share, 2.31 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 20.6% first-read share. Douglas has had plenty of flashes when on the field, with a 70-yard and two-touchdown outing against the Jets and 94 receiving yards earlier this season against the Raiders. Douglas is flex-viable, but Detroit has been tougher against perimeter wide receivers in recent weeks. Over their last five games, Detroit has held perimeter wide receivers to the 11th-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity.

Josh Downs is the WR55 in fantasy points per game. Last week, he saved his fantasy day with a score, but it was his fifth game in a row without surpassing 50 receiving yards. When Rashee Rice has been a full-time player, Xavier Worthy has had a 15.1% target share with 0.62 YPRR, six red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 19.4% first-read share. He hasn't surpassed 25 receiving yards in any of those four games. I don't have any faith left in Worthy. I understand he surpassed 70 receiving yards against the Raiders and Chargers' secondaries with Rice out, but with Rice in the lineup, he has been a ghost. As a limited-snap player this week, Tyson would be an easy sit if active.

Sit Thomas until the usage picks up.
