Sam LaPorta has been quiet over the last two games with only 51 total receiving yards, but this is the eruption spot for LaPorta. Sammy Ballgame is the TE6 in fantasy points per game. LaPorta has a 15.7% target share with 1.72 YPRR, nine red zone targets, one deep target, and a 16.6% first-read share. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the ninth-most yards per target, the second-most receiving touchdowns, and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Tyler Warren is the TE5 in fantasy points per game. Warren has a 22.3% target share with 1.26 YPRR, five red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 21.8% first-read share. He'll need a touchdown this week to finish as a TE1 because one of the few things Dallas has been doing well is defending tight ends. Over their last five games, they have allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Travis Kelce keeps motoring along as a low-end TE1 as the TE11 in fantasy points per game. Kelce has a 17.7% target share with 2.23 YPRR, three red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 20% first-read share. Kelce has had at least 50 receiving yards in five of seven games this season. Kelce should produce as a TE1 again this week. Over the last five games, New York has allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity (tied) to tight ends.

After last week's monster game, Harold Fannin is the TE8 in fantasy points per game. Fannin has a 19.1% target share with 1.72 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 19.6% first-read share. This week, he'll face a Saints defense that has the second-highest single high rate in the NFL (65%). Against single-high, Fannin has a 22% TPRR (second on the team) with 1.91 YPRR. Fannin should post another strong TE1 stat line this week. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 5, Kyle Pitts has been the TE6 in fantasy points per game. In those four games, Pitts has had a 66.9% route share, a 17.5% target share, 1.40 YPRR, six red zone targets, and a 21.2% first-read share. Cincy still can't stop tight ends. They have been hopeless against them, which makes Pitts a strong start this week with huge upside. In their last five games, Cincy has allowed the most yards per target and the second-most receiving yards to tight ends.

T.J. Hockenson is the TE10 in fantasy points per game. Hockenson has an 18.7% target share with 2.22 YPRR, seven red zone targets, and a 20.6% first-read share. He could easily be a TE1 again this week against a defense that, over its last five games, has allowed the fifth-most yards per target to tight ends.

After a slow start, since Week 4, Tucker Kraft has been the TE6 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 4, Kraft has had a 70.8% route share, a 17% target share, 1.77 YPRR, eight red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 20% first-read share. Kraft isn't likely to have a blow-up game this week, but with his touchdown equity in the Packers' passing attack, he could easily be a solid TE1. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the 11th-most receiving fantasy points per game and ranked 18th in yards per target against tight ends.

After last week's limited volume performance, Brenton Strange has fallen to TE15 in fantasy points per game. Strange has a 17.4% target share with 2.26 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and an 18.9% first-read share. Strange could easily bounce back this week as a strong TE1. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the 14th-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Dalton Kincaid is the TE8 in fantasy points per game. He had a big bounce-back game last week as the TE4 for the week. That was the first game he had crossed 12 PPR points since Week 2. Overall, he has a 61.6% route share, a 17.1% target share, 2.75 YPRR, six red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 21.4% first-read share. This feels like another down week incoming for Kincaid. This week, he'll face a Vikings secondary that has the fourth-highest two-high rate in the NFL (64%). Against two-high, Kincaid has a 20% TPRR with 1.44 YPRR. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 6, Dallas Goedert has been the TE19 in fantasy points per game. Goedert has had a 15.4% target share with 1.65 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 24% first-read share. This week he's a must-sit. Over their last five games, the Giants have held tight ends to the third-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Greg Dulcich has emerged as a big part of the Miami passing offense over his last three games. Since Week 5, Dulcich has had a 62.6% route share, a 20% target share, 2.68 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 25.5% first-read share. Dulcich is a wonderful streaming option this week, and he could be a TE1 this week. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the third-most yards per target, the most receiving fantasy points per game, and the most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Mike Gesicki is the TE12 in fantasy points per game. Overall, he has a 47.8% snap rate, a 54.7% route share, a 9% target share, 1.53 YPRR, five red zone targets, two deep targets, and an 11.1% first-read share. What has propped up his fantasy value is his insane touchdown runout, as he has six scores this season. Last week, without Erick All, Gesicki did see a jump in his playing time with a 71.7% route share and 67.1% snap rate. I expect those numbers to carry over into Week 9. Gesicki is an interesting streaming option this week. The coverage matchup is in his favor, but Atlanta has been tough against tight ends, so he has a wide range of outcomes this week. Atlanta has the third-highest rate of single high (60.7%). Against single-high, Gesicki has seen his TPRR increase to 20% with 2.00 YPRR. However, over their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the 11th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends while ranking 16th in yards per target. Gesicki could be a TE1 this week or disappoint. It's a coin flip.

Since Week 6, Chig Okonkwo has been the TE21 in fantasy points per game with one TE1 outing (TE11). In those two games, Okonkwo has had a 15.9% target share with 1.58 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 21.3% first-read share. This isn't the matchup to consider streaming Okonkwo. Over their last five games, the Rams have held tight ends to the 11th-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Dalton Schultz is the TE18 in fantasy points per game, but that ranking is really just carried by his outing against Cincy. Schultz hasn't had double-digit PPR points in any other game this season. Schultz has a 57% snap rate, a 62.1% route share, a 17.7% target share with 1.91 YPRR, five red zone targets, four deep targets, and an 18% first-read share. Schultz is on the streaming radar this week. Across their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the most yards per target to tight ends while giving up the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 3, Michael Mayer has been the TE9 in fantasy points per game. In those six games, Mayer has had a 13.3% target share, 1.83 YPRR, only two deep targets, one red zone target, and an 11.9% first-read share. He has been efficient with limited volume and doesn't have much high cholesterol usage in this offense. Even if I could get past all that, he has a tough matchup this week. The 49ers have been tough on tight ends. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. Sit Mayer.

Ok, well, here we go. I'm doing the Tyler Higbee thing again. There's no way that this backfires, right? (Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen say hi) Since Week 3, Higbee has been the TE21 in fantasy points per game. In his last three games, he has failed each week to surpass five PPR points. This is after three strong games in a row in Weeks 3-5. Since Week 3, he has had a 12.6% target share with 1.47 YPRR, two red zone targets, and a 15% first-read share. Higbee is a solid streaming option again this week (crossing my fingers). Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity.

Juwan Johnson has seen his role decline. In his last two games, Johnson has had only a 56.8% snap rate, 56.2% route share, 4.4% target share, and a 7% first-read share. Over their last five games, Cleveland has ranked 15th in receiving fantasy points per game against tight ends while giving up the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. This would put Johnson on the streaming radar this week, but I'm not starting him in most formats. I need to see his role rebound before I'm comfortable plugging him into a starting lineup.

AJ Barner is a low-end tight end streaming option this week. It's all based on the matchup. Barner has a 12.3% target share with 0.96 YPRR, seven red zone targets, and a 13.7% first-read share. Barner is the TE27 in fantasy points per game, with only one game this season with double-digit PPR points. Over their last five games, Arizona has allowed the 14th-most receiving fantasy points per game and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

In Weeks 4-8, Mark Andrews has been the TE34 in fantasy points per game. He had eclipsed six PPR points only once during that span. Since Week 4, he has had a 15.1% target share with 0.81 YPRR, six red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 16.8% first-read share. Volume and red zone equity haven't been the issue. Andrews just isn't doing anything with the opportunities. I think this week is more of the same. Sit Andrews. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Jake Ferguson sustained an ankle injury last week. He didn't practice until Friday of this week. He was a limited participant on Friday and has been listed as questionable. Last week, he played only four snaps. In the two games before that, his usage had begun to decline. In those games, he had a 54.1% snap rate, a 51.2% route share, a 4.9% target share, and only one first-read target. Ferguson's usage and playing time were already worrisome, but if he's active this week and playing through an injury, I don't see his snap rate improving. Sit Ferguson this week.

Hunter Henry (foot) didn't practice until Friday this week, when he managed a limited practice. He has been listed as questionable this week. Henry is the TE20 in fantasy points per game with a 13.8% target share, 1.93 YPRR, five red zone targets, one deep target, and a 15.2% first-read share. He's an easy sit this week. Over their last five games, Green Bay has allowed the ninth-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Jeffery Simmons, or the Jeffe, as Caleb Williams proclaimed on the sidelines, went off for three solos, three assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Simmons' addition was hailed as a seismic one here last week, but now the non-IDP fan has seen the proof. Simmons is up to five sacks on the season and has a sack in two of his last three games. Now playing for a team expected to be in neutral or positive gamescipts most games, Simmons is going to have more pass rush opportunities than he has seen in a long time, perhaps ever. Fire Simmons up as a top-15 play going forward.

Greg Rousseau showed up in Week 8, racking up two solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. Now up to seven sacks on the season, the sack was the Bills edge rusher's first since Week 3. Rousseau remains an elite option, but his long power outage makes him more of a top-12 option than the top-five option his current sack count suggests. Treat him as such for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football.

Maxx Crosby showed up in Week 8, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Crosby has been a shell of himself this season, recording just three sacks on the season, with this being his first full sack since all the way back in Week 1. He remains in the top-15 mix due to his obvious talent and past production, but he can no longer be counted as a top-five, or even top-three weekly lock he was once considered. Tap Crosby as a DL1 play for a plus Week 9 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Josh Hines-Allen has struggled for IDP managers this season but showed some signs of life in Week 8, registering four solos, one assist, 0.5 sacks, and one tackle for loss. Hines-Allen has just two sacks on the season, but has managed three spike weeks total in his seven games played, suggesting that not all has been lost with his sack outage. JHA is a top-25 option who can be bumped up in plus matchups. He has one of those this Thursday against the Joe Fagano led Baltimore Ravens. Treat him as a top-15 play, thanks to the tasty matchup.

George Karlaftis showed up in Week 8, tallying two solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and three passes defended. It was the second sack of the season for Furious George, who continues to rack up the pressures but does not always leave games with the sack total his pressure rate suggests he could. Still, Karlaftis makes for a fine DL3 with weekly DL2 upside. Treat him as such for a plus Week 9 matchup against the New York Jets.

Tuli Tuipulotu stepped up in Week 8, tallying three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The QB takedown was just his third sack of the season, and his first full sack since Week 3. Tuli was always expected to be a sacks-in-bunches type of IDP player, but his sack count through eight weeks drops him down to the DL3 conversation. It is a precipitous drop for the former DL1 option, but he should still be started in all competitive leagues. Tap him as a top-30 option for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Houston Texans.

Quinnen Williams was back at it in Week 8, exploding for four solos, three assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. It was the third straight spike week for Quinnen, who now has four sacks in his last three games. All of Williams' five sacks have come in four of his last five contests. Quinnen is back on the DT1/DL2 radar with his recent surge and should be counted as just that for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Boye Mafe stayed hot in Week 8, racking up four solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Boye has now recorded a spike week in three of his last four games and is up to 5.5 sacks, with at least one sack in each of those four games. Mafe needs to be counted as a top-25 option while he is cooking. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Lukas Van Ness showed up in Week 8, tallying three solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Van Ness is up to 4.5 sacks on the season, with one in two of his last three games. LVN could lose snaps with the return of Micah Parsons and emergence of Dani Dennis-Sutton, but can be counted as a strong DL3 option for Week 9. Start the Packers edge rusher where needed for a plus Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots.

Dexter Lawrence stayed hot in Week 8, tallying four solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. It is the second straight spike week for the defensive tackle, who is now up to five sacks on the season, with all five coming in four of his last five games. Count Lawrence as a locked-in DT1/DL3 play, who can be leaned on as DL2 in a pinch. Start Dexter everywhere for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons in Spain.

Travon Walker showed up in Week 8, reeling off two solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Travon is up to three sacks on the season, which is a solid number, but keeps him stuck in the DL3 conversation instead of the DL2 discussion one would hope he eventually developed into. Count Walker as a top-30 option for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday night.

Jalen Carter was back at it in Week 8, racking up two solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. The sack was the fourth of the season for Jalen, who has recorded three of his four sacks in two of his last four contests. The Eagles are a dumpster fire, but that has not stopped Carter from being a menace on the interior of the defensive line. Tap Jalen as a DT1/DL3 play with confidence.

Josh Sweat was back at it in Week 8, tallying two solos, four assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Sweat has started to heat up since he has gotten healthier and is now up to three sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of his last five games. Treat Sweat as a borderline top-25 option during the byes for as long as he is cooking. The Cardinals edge rusher should be rostered in all competitive leagues.

Josh Uche stepped up in Week 8, notching four solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Uche has just two sacks on the season but is logging heavy snaps on the edge for the Dolphins, making him an ideal bye week filler type. He is still more of a DL4 than a DL3, but is a strong option if you are dealing with a bye-week crunch. Start Uche where needed for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

Chop Robinson stepped up in Week 8, racking up three solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Chop is now up to fo four sacks on the season, with three of them coming in his last two games played. Robinson remains more DL3 than DL2 despite getting hot production wise, but should be rostered in all competitive leagues following his showing against New England. Add and start Chop where possible ahead of a plus Week 9 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

K'Lavon Chaisson stepped up in Week 8, notching three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Chaisson is up to 3.5 sacks on the season, with all of them coming in his last six contests. K'Lavon is a solid, if unspectacular DL3 option during the byes, and should be treated as such ahead of a plus Week 9 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Dorance Armstrong showed up in Week 8, recording four solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. The sack was the first of the season for Armstrong, who is part of a maddening edge rotation in Washington. There is, of course, upside here, but with K'Lavon Chaisson, Charles Omenihu, and Odafe Oweh all playing more snaps than Dorance most weeks, the ceiling is capped, and the floor is virtually bottomless. Keep him rostered in 20+ team leagues, but those in 12 team leagu
es should look elsewhere for Week 9.

Josaiah Stewart was excellent in Week 8, tallying two solos, four assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. The sack was the second of the season for the Rams edge rusher. Stewart belongs on 32 team league rosters but should still not be on the radar for those who play in leagues with fewer than 20 teams. Look elsewhere for Week 9.

Devonte Wyatt showed up in Week 8, racking up two solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. It was the third sack of the season for Wyatt, who has seen all three of his sacks come in two of his last four games. Tap Devonte as a DT2 who can serve as a DL4/5 bye week filler type if you find yourself in a crunch.

Malcolm Roach was at it again in Week 8, notching three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Now up to 3.5 sacks on the season, with a sack in each of his last two games, Roach can be counted as a borderline DT1 target for Week 9, thanks to a plus matchup against the Carolina Panthers. Roach can also be viewed as a potential DL5 bye week filler type if you find yourself in a pinch.

Dani Dennis-Sutton impressed in Week 8, racking up two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. DDS is now up to 2.5 sacks on the season, with one sack in two of his last four games. Dani will not see his role increase any time soon due to Micah Parsons being scheduled to return to practice this week, but will share the field with both Parsons and Lukas Van Ness as he kicks inside on some snaps, where one of his 2.5 sacks has come from this season. DDS should be rostered in deeper leagues and all dynasty leagues.

Corey Durden stepped up in Week 8, notching two solos, two assists, 1.5 sacks, and two tackles for loss. The sacks were the first of the season for Durden, who is now on the DT3 radar for IDP purposes. He is not yet someone to consider in DL leagues unless you play in a 32-team league.

Barryn Sorrell stepped up in Week 8, tallying four solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the first full sack of the season for Sorrell, who is up to 1.5 on the year. It was a sack party for the Packers against Carolina, but Sorrell, among others, is expected to see his snaps scaled back once Micah Parsons is activated and returns to the lineup. Sorrell should not yet be on radars outside of 20+ team leagues.

Charles Omenihu stepped up in Week 8, recording two solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. It was the first sack of the season for Omenihu, who returned from a two game layoff after being hurt early in Week 4. The veteran edge rusher should be considered more DL4 than DL3, at least for now, but is worth considering if you find yourself in a bye week crunch. Start him where needed for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Jarran Reed showed up in Week 8, tallying four solos, three assists, and two tackles for loss. Reed has just one sack on the season but has two games with at least seven combined tackles, highlighting why he has remained a DT1 option with just one QB takedown. Look elsewhere in DL leagues, but start Reed confidently in DT formats.

Shy Tuttle was back at it in Week 8, racking up four solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. It was the second sack of the season for Tuttle, who has hovered around the 35-40 percent snap share mark for most of the season. Tuttle now has a sack in back-to-back games, making him a DT2 option with both Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw lost for the season. Fire Tuttle up as a top-24 DT option in DT leagues. Look elsewhere for Week 9 in DL leagues.

Wesley Bailey stepped up in Week 8, tallying two solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. The sack was the second of the season for Bailey, who had hovered around 30 percent of the snaps in prior weeks before seeing 52.5 percent against the Chargers. Bailey will see his role reduced when Myles Garrett is finally healthy, but makes for a solid 32 team league stash. For those in normal-sized leagues, Bailey should not be on your radar for Week 9.

Ernest Jones stayed hot in Week 8, racking up five solos, eight assists, and one pass defended. Jones has been elite this season and checks into Week 9 as the LB7 in fppg. Fire the Seahawks linebacker up as a top-five option as long as he is cooking.

Blake Cashman was at it again in Week 8, racking up five solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. The RB1 in fppg, Cashman has five spike weeks and one splash week in his seven games played. Continue to count Cashman as a top-five option for Week 9 against Buffalo.

Alex Singleton stayed hot in Week 8, racking up six solos, eight assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Singleton is on absolute fire, recording a splash week in back-to-back games. Singleton has been the most consistent option at the position and checks into Week 9 as the Lb2 in fppg. Count Singleton as a top-five option until further notice.

Jordyn Brooks was back at it in Week 8, reeling off six solos and five assists. Brooks has started to heat up, recording a spike week in three of his last four games. His recent production puts him back in the top-15 mix for Week 8 and beyond. Start Brooks with confidence for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

Fred Warner was excellent in Week 7, tallying six solos, seven assists, and two tackles for loss. Warner now has four spike weeks and one splash week to his name, keeping him firmly in the top-10 mix. The LB3 overall in fantasy points through seven weeks of action, Warner is an easy top-five play while he is cooking. Start the 49ers superstar linebacker everywhere regardless of opponent, including this week against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Jamien Sherwood stepped up in Week 8, racking up five solos and nine assists. Sherwood has officially heard up for fantasy managers, recording a spike or splash week in four of his last five games. Count Jamien as a top-15 option as long as he is steaming. Start him everywhere for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Roquan Smith stepped up in Week 8, racking up six solos, five assists, one forced fumble, and two passes defended. Roquan has been consistent but has just one splash week and two spike weeks on the season. With that said, he had three near misses and has started to heat up lately with five or more solos in three of his last four games. Tap the Ravens linebacker as a top-15 option for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Foyesade Oluokun was excellent in Week 8, tallying five solos, four assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Oluokun has three spike weeks and one splash week in seven games, keeping him in the top-12 mix for Week 9 and beyond. Start Foyesade with confidence.

Nate Landman stepped up in Week 8, tallying seven solos, one assist, and one tackle for loss. Landman has recorded a spike or splash week in three straight, with six or more solos in each. Count the Rams linebacker as a top-12 option for a plus Week 9 matchup against Washington.

Christian Elliss was at it again in Week 8, notching three solos, six assists. 0.5 sacks, and two tackles for loss. Elliss has recorded consecutive spike weeks, solidifying him as a strong LB3 option even outside of the byes. Count Elliss as a top-36 option for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Devin Bush showed up in Week 8, tallying five solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Bush has just two spike weeks to his name, but also has two near misses he can confidently be counted as a quality LB3 with LB2 upside. Treat him as such for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Arvell Reese has been lights out for the New York Giants, most recently racking up five solos, two assists, 0.5 sacks, and one tackle for loss in Week 7. Arvell has two spike weeks, two splash weeks, and two near misses on his resume through seven weeks of action, vaulting him up to LB6 overall on the season heading into the team's Week 8 bye. Count Reese as a top-10 option, period.

Eric Wilson stepped up in Week 8, tallying seven solos, four assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. It was the second splash week of the season for Wilson, who has been pretty quiet in his other contests. No longer a LB2 consideration, his production proves that he remains a high upside LB3 play due to his incredible peaks. Add Wilson where needed ahead of a plus Week 9 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Jeremiah Trotter was excellent in Week 8, notching six solos and four assists. Trotter got the start with Jihaad Campbell ruled out and appears poised to get at least another start or two with Campbell dealing with a hamstring injury. Trotter is a top-36 option for as long as Jihaad is sidelined. Start Trotter everywhere.

Mack Wilson stepped up in Week 8, posting three solos, five assists, and two tackles for loss. Wilson is a bye week filler LB5 type, but fresh off a spike week with the byes at hand, he becomes worth consideration for your LB3 to flex2 spot. Start the Cardinals linebacker where needed.

Micah McFadden stepped up in a big way for the New York Giants in Week 7, tallying 10 solos and two assists as the veteran did his best Tremaine Edmunds impression. Edmunds has been lost for the season with a shoulder injury, which means McFadden is set to get plenty of burn for the Giants. Treat Micah as an instant LB3 play who has LB2 upside in this scheme, as long as he is playing starter-level snaps.

Ty'Ron Hopper was excellent in Week 8, racking up six solos, two assists, one sack, one interception, and three passes defended on 97 percent of the snaps. Hopper and Isiaiah McDuffie are both playing starter snaps while Zaire Franklin remains sidelined with a leg injury, making Hopper an easy LB3 play during the byes. And as his production against Carolina suggests, he has weekly LB2 upside. Hopper should be rostered in all competitive leagues ahead of a plus Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots.

Shemar James stepped up in Week 8, racking up five solos, four assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Shemar has recorded four or more solos in three straight games, registering five or more in each of the last two. It was the first spike week of the season for James, who has taken over MIKE duties from Jaishawn Barham and is starting alongside DeMarvion Overshown. Treat Shemar as an LB3 with LB2 upside going forward.

Alex Anzalone was excellent in Week 8, notching three solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, two interceptions, and two passes defended. Anzalone had just one spike week all season prior to his Week 8 breakout, but the production puts him on the LB3 radar during the byes. Tap the Buccaneers linebacker as a top-36 option for what should be a busy afternoon against the Chicago Bears.

Henry To'oTo'o stepped up in Week 7, racking three solos, seven assists, 0.5 sacks, and two tackles for loss. It was the first spike week of the season for Henry To'oTo'o, who played just his second full game of the season. To'oTo'o has proven top-25 prowess, but should be counted as more of an LB3 option until he shows enough consistency to be trusted alongside others who have been producing for more than a third of the season. Fire the Texans linebacker up as a top-30 option for a tasty Week 9 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Dre Greenlaw stepped up in Week 7, notching four solos and eight assists. It was the second spike week of the season for the 49ers linebacker, who has recorded four or more solos in three of his five full games. Greenlaw should be rostered in all competitive leagues with the bye and suspension behind him. Fire him up as a top-30 option for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders. Add and start Greenlaw where needed.

Andrew Van Ginkel stepped up in Week 8, tallying two solos, two assists, 2.5 sacks, and two tackles for loss. AVG is now up to 6.5 sacks on the season, with at least a half sack in five of his seven games. Van Ginkel had three spike weeks under his belt prior to this splash week and checks in as the DL6 in fppg through eight weeks of action. Fire the veteran edge rusher up as a top-20 option as long as he is cooking, including this week against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football.

CJ Allen got his first NFL start in Week 8 and responded with four solos, six assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Allen has taken over MIKE duties and should quickly become a top-15 mainstay in IDP. For now, treat him as an upside top-20 option. Congratulations to those of you who had the roster space and patience to hold onto him this long in redraft leagues; for the rest of us, the scramble for a waiver wire linebacker with top-12 potential begins.

Gabe Jacas stepped up in Week 8, racking up one solo, two assists, 1.5 sacks, and one tackle for loss. Jacas is up to three sacks on the season and has been playing a steady role while Harold Landry remains sidelined. Jacas suffered a knee injury against Miami, meaning fantasy managers will want to monitor his game status ahead of Week 9. Treat Gabe as a DL4 with DL3 bye week filler appeal where needed.

Zaven Collins stepped up in Week 8, posting three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. The sack is the second of the season for Collins, who continues to share snaps with Josh Sweat, Baron Browning, and Jordan Burch. Collins is nothing more than a bye week filler DL5 type, but should remain rostered in deeper leagues as just that. Start him where needed for Week 9.

Brenton Cox stepped up in Week 8, notching two solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one fumble recovery. It was the first sack of the season for Cox, who appears poised to see his snaps scaled back once Micah Parsons returns. There is dynasty appeal here due to his age, but that is just for those in 32 team leagues. All others should look elsewhere for Week 9.

Caden Curry showed up in Week 8, tallying five solos, two assists, and one fumble recovery. Curry is a plus defender against the run and managed a spike week without a sack to his name yet this season. Curry could become a 12-team option if he sees his role expand, but for now should be targeted in 20+ team leagues.

Evan Williams continued his breakout season, recording seven solos and three assists. Williams has been an absolute IDP monster in 2026, going from an inconsistent but flashing DB3 to the cream of the crop among DB1s. Treat Williams as a top-three option, period.

Kyle Hamilton stayed hot in Week 9, reeling off five solos, two assists, and one tackle for loss. Hamilton remains an elite DB1 option and has registered six spike weeks in his last seven games. Fire up the Ravens do-it-all safety as a top-five option for Thursday Night Football.

Jeremy Chinn was at it again in Week 8, racking up four solos, six assists, one interception, and one pass defended. The Raiders safety has caught fire over his last four games and remains a comfortable weekly DB1 play. Treat him as such for a plus Week 9 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Dane Belton was at it again in Week 8, tallying eight solos, four assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. The DB6 in fppg since Week 4, Belton has recorded four spike weeks in his five games. Fire the Jets safety up as an easy top-20 play for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Quentin Lake was excellent in Week 8, notching two solos, five assists, one interception, and two passes defended. Lake has three spike weeks and one splash week under his belt and remains a strong DB1 option regardless of opponent. The DB6 on the season, fire Lake up an easy top-10 play for a plus Week 9 matchup against Washington.

Jordan Battle was excellent in Week 8, recording nine solos, three assists, and two passes defended. Battle has caught fire for IDP managers, registering two splash weeks in his last three contests. Now the DB10 in fppg, count Battle as an easy top-12 option for Week 9 and beyond.

Kendal Daniels was excellent in Week 8, racking up six solos and seven assists. Daniels has recorded a spike or splash week in four straight games. He has registered six or more solos in all four of those games and needs to be counted as a top-20 option as long as he remains on fire. Start Kendal everywhere for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals in Spain.

Josh Metellus showed up in Week 8, tallying five solos, eight assists, and one pass defended. It was the second spike week of the season for Metellus, who remains more DB3 than DB2, at least for now. Treat him as such for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football.

Devon Witherspoon stepped up in Week 8, tallying five solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Devon has just two spike weeks on the season, but remains a DB3 option due to his easy DB2 upside. Tap Witherspoon as a DB3 option against the Arizona Cardinals.

Jacob Parrish stayed hot in Week 8, racking up four solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, one interception, and two passes defended. Parrish has been on fire for IDP managers, recording four spike weeks in his last five games. The Buccaneers corner needs to be counted as a DB2 play while he is smoking. Make the add in all competitive leagues.

Nick Cross stepped up Week 8, tallying five solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Cross has two spike weeks in his four games played. Cross is a top-15 option when he is healthy, but should be counted as more of a top-20 option for Week 9 against the Los Angeles Rams.

Cole Bishop was back at it in Week 8, registering two solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Bishop had been quiet through the first few weeks of the season but has now recorded two spike weeks in his last three games, putting him in the mix as a borderline DB2 option. Tap Bishop as a top-30 option for a plus Week 9 option for Monday Night Football against the Minnesota Vikings.

Kevin Byard stepped up in Week 8, racking up four solos, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended. It was the first spike week of the season for Byard, who has dropped down to the DB3 conversation. Tap the Patriots safety as a top-36 option where needed.

Andrew Wingard returned from injury in Week 8, racking up six solos and one assist. Wingard has been excellent when he has been healthy this season, with two spike weeks and one near miss in his five games played. Treat the Cardinals safety as a top-25 option until he cools down.

Andrew Mukuba was excellent in Week 8, tallying seven solos, two assists, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Mukuba is now on more radars thanks to the spike week, but it is recording four or more solos in three straight games that has elevated him into the top-25 conversation, at least during the byes. Count the Eagles safety as just that for a plus Week 9 matchup against the New York Giants.

Carlton Davis showed up in Week 8, posting seven solos and two assists. Davis has recorded seven solos twice in his four games played, making him an intriguing CB2 with CB1 upside. His ceiling puts him on the DB4/DB5 radar, but he is more someone you want clogging your bench while producing than someone you want to plug into lineups until he shows a little more.

Byron Murphy was back at it in Week 8, tallying eight solos and two assists. Murphy has been one of the best tackling corners since he entered the league, and production like this serves as a reminder. The Vikings corner has three spike weeks and one splash week in seven games played and is an easy CB1/DB3 play for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Malaki Starks was back at it in Week 8, racking up five solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. It was the fourth spike week of the season for Starks, who has recorded five or more solos in three of his last five games. Treat the Ravens safety as a top-25 option for a plus Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football.

Devon Key was excellent in Week 8, racking up five solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Key has impressed enough with five solos in two of his last three games to keep stashed, and should be plugged into lineups with Hufanga a surprise inactive for Week 9. Start Key everywhere as DB3 with DB2 upside.

Pat Surtain was back in action in Week 8 and posted seven solos, one assist, and one pass defended. Surtain was sidelined for three games, but didn't miss a beat in his return, recording his second spike week of the season. Surtain is still more of a CB league play, but can be plugged in lineups in INT-heavy DB leagues. Start Surtain where needed.

Marco Wilson stepped off the practice squad to record six solos, two assists, and two passes defended. Wilson got the start with Will Lee sidelined, and with Lee missing the first two practices of the week, Wilson may get another start. With that said, Wilson should not be a consideration outside of deeper CB leagues. He makes for a fine CB3 option, but probably should not even be on rosters outside of max bench 20+ team leagues. Look elsewhere in DB leagues and 12 team CB leagues.

Rayuan Lane was excellent in Week 8, notching one solo, three assists, one interception, three passes defended, and one touchdown. It was the first splash week of the season for Lane, who is primarily a backup to Antonio Johnson and Eric Murray, but with Murray lost for the season with an elbow injury, Lane is now expected to be a full-time starter. Count Rayuan as a top-36 option going forward. Make the add in all competitive leagues ahead of a plus Week 9 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.

Eric Stokes stepped up in Week 8, reeling off seven solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. Stokes is a solid CB2 option during the bye weeks, but should not be a consideration in DB leagues. Treat him as such for a plus Week 9 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Zakee Wheatley stepped up in Week 8, reeling off four solos, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Wheatley has stepped into the box role for the Panthers with Tre'Von Moehrig playing deep, and has responded with four solos in three of his six games played. Treat Zakee as a DB3 option as long as he is rolling.
